title: Clinical and Laboratory Characteristics, Disease Activity, and Disease Damage: A Saudi National Lupus Cohort Study.
abstract: Background: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) disease activity and damage assessments are crucial for understanding the disease burden across different lupus populations. This study aims to describe the disease characteristics, treatment, and disease activity and damage in the Saudi national prospective SLE cohort. Methods: Saudi SLE patients over 18 years of age were recruited prospectively from January 2020 to December 2023 from the national prospective cohort of SLE, Saudi Arabia. Data retrieved included patients' sociodemographic characteristics, medical history, clinical manifestations and laboratory features, comorbidities, and medications at baseline visit, first follow-up at 3 months, and subsequent follow-up visits every 6 months. The SLE disease activity index 2000 (SLEDAI-2K) and Systemic Lupus International Collaboration Clinics/American College of Rheumatology (SLICC/ACR) damage index (SDI) scores were computed at baseline and follow-up visits following a standardized protocol. The generalized linear model was employed to assess organ damage based on the SDI scores. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was performed to assess major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) and mortality. The Cox regression model was used to adjust for lupus disease and cardiovascular risk factors. Results: The mean age at SLE diagnosis of the 488 patients was 30.6 ± 11.9 years. The mean SLEDAI-2K and SDI scores were 8.0 ± 7.2 and 0.61 ± 1.1, respectively. The SLEDAI-2K scores declined initially and increased in follow-up visits. The SDI scores also increased at the follow-up visits. Musculoskeletal organ damage was found in 10.7% of the patients, neuropsychiatric damage in 9.2%, skin damage in 6.1%, renal damage in 5.9%, and cardiovascular damage in 4.4%. The parameters analyzed for predicting organ damage progression did not reach statistical significance, which may be due to the limited statistical power of the study and may not reflect an absence of relationship. Oral prednisolone was administered to 43.1% of the patients and hydroxychloroquine to 89.2%. The Kaplan-Meier 5- and 10-year survival rates were 99% and 98%, respectively. The initial findings using Cox regression analysis indicated that a longer SLE duration is protective of MACEs. However, a sensitivity analysis with a time-dependent approach did not retain significance of the SLE duration on the outcome of early MACEs. There was a trend of obesity and earlier MACE occurrence. Conclusions: Lupus disease activity and disease damage increased from the baseline visit over time. The most prevalent organ damage included musculoskeletal, neuropsychiatric, renal, and cardiovascular systems, consistent with previous studies. Time-invariant analysis showed an association between a longer SLE duration and MACEs, but such findings did not retain significance with a time-dependent approach, which may be due to immortal time bias. Obesity was found to contribute to early MACEs.

title: The Multidimensional Pathogenesis of Susceptibility to Depression in Sjögren's Syndrome: An Integrated Approach from Immune-Inflammatory to Psychosocial Factors.
abstract: Sjögren's syndrome is a chronic systemic autoimmune disease with primary (pSS) and secondary forms. Epidemiological evidence suggests a higher prevalence of depressive symptoms and depression in pSS than in the general population, indicating possible disease-specific susceptibility. The underlying mechanisms remain unclear, limiting early identification and targeted intervention. This narrative review examines five domains of depression susceptibility in pSS: inflammatory pathways, neuroendocrine regulation, the gut-brain axis, medication effects, and psychosocial factors. Interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-α, and interferon-α may contribute by activating the indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase-kynurenine pathway, downregulating brain-derived neurotrophic factor, and inhibiting hippocampal neurogenesis. Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysfunction may provide a neuroendocrine link, whereas gut microbial imbalance may affect emotional regulation through immune and neural signaling. Glucocorticoids, hydroxychloroquine, and calcineurin inhibitors may increase neuropsychiatric risk through multiple pathways. Somatic symptoms and social stress may reinforce a psychosocial vicious cycle. Much of the mechanistic evidence comes from major depressive disorder, animal models, or in vitro studies; causality has not been established in pSS. The proposed multidimensional model is hypothetical and offers a framework for early screening and targeted intervention in pSS with depression.

title: Hydroxychloroquine alleviates unexplained recurrent spontaneous abortion through IL-8-mediated decidual macrophage polarization and facilitates trophoblast invasion.
abstract: Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ), a classic immunomodulatory drug, is generally safe during pregnancy. However, its effects and regulatory mechanisms in unexplained recurrent spontaneous abortion (URSA) remain unclear. This study investigated whether HCQ affects pregnancy outcomes, decidual macrophage polarization, and trophoblast function in URSA, with a particular focus on interleukin-8 (IL-8). A URSA mouse model was established to evaluate the effects of different doses of HCQ on pregnancy outcomes, decidual macrophages (DMs) polarization, trophoblast function and placental IL-8 expression. In vitro, decidual stromal cell (DSC)-DMs and DSC-trophoblast co-culture systems were used to assess the effects of HCQ and the IL-8 inhibitor repertaxin on NF-κB, DMs polarization and trophoblast migration and invasion. Network pharmacology was used to identify potential HCQ-related targets, and molecular docking was performed to assess the potential interaction between HCQ and IL-8. In URSA mice, HCQ improved pregnancy outcomes, reducing embryo resorption and increasing embryo and placental weights, with maximal effects at the medium dose. HCQ increased placental CK7 expression, particularly at the medium dose, and reduced the DMs M1/M2 ratio in a dose-dependent manner. Placental IL-8 protein levels were markedly decreased in all HCQ-treated groups. In the co-culture system, HCQ-treated DSCs reduced the DMs M1/M2 ratio, and this effect was further enhanced by combined HCQ and repertaxin treatment. HCQ inhibited trophoblast migration and invasion, and the inhibition was more pronounced after combined treatment with repertaxin. HCQ downregulated NF-κB expression in DMs and trophoblasts; this inhibition was more prominent when combined with repertaxin. Network pharmacology identified IL-8 as a potential key target, while molecular docking showed a predicted HCQ-IL-8 binding energy of -5.7 kcal/mol. In conclusion, HCQ modulates DSC-derived IL-8 and NF-κB signaling, with associated changes in trophoblast invasion, decidual macrophage polarization, and pregnancy outcomes in URSA mice.
